title: Halcyon FX (MT5 EA): first 4 weeks of live results, warts and all
author: Teh_Eno
selftext:
**Disclosure:** I built this EA and sell it.

It's AI-assisted: the EA finds setups with its own rules, then a local bridge asks Claude (an AI model) to confirm or veto certain entries before they're placed. The AI can only block trades, never create them.

Halcyon has been about a year in development, through many iterations. It's been running live since mid-September on a small account (about $1.08k, 0.01–0.03 lots), with several builds shipped along the way (the current one since 10 Oct). Here are real results as % return and profit factor, which are fair for any account size:

* 14–19 Sep: PF 1.26, +1.00%
* 21–26 Sep: PF 0.16, −3.52%
* 28 Sep–3 Oct: PF 1.08, +0.22%
* 5–10 Oct: PF 4.44, +3.12%

That's roughly +0.7% over 4 weeks, with one losing week. PF has risen two weeks running and the latest week was the best, but samples are small (4–10 trades a week), so treat it as early data, not proof. I'll post every week, losing weeks included.

Site: [halcyon-fx.vercel.app](https://halcyon-fx.vercel.app/)

*Not financial advice. FX trading carries substantial risk of loss.*

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: letting claude only veto and never create entries is a sane setup. on the numbers though, at 4 to 10 trades a week one good week swings PF from 0.16 to 4.44, so the rising trend says very little until you're past a hundred or so trades.

replies.author: BlackOpz
replies.body:
> so the rising trend says very little until you're past a hundred or so trades

Yep, 30 trades can give you a 'signal' (if it's trash for 30 - it's prob trash) but you need 100+ to even 'think' you have an edge. Then... Congratulations!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: yeah, 30 bad trades is enough to kill one, 30 good ones isn't enough to trust it. that asymmetry is the annoying bit. I'd also split the 100 by week, since at 4 to 10 a week one news week can carry the whole count.

replies.author: Teh_Eno
replies.body:
Agreed on both. Veto-only (block, never create) is deliberate on LIVE — Claude can only refuse setups the EA already wanted.

And yeah, with only a handful of trades a week the PF can jump around hard. One good week doesn’t make a trend. I’m treating the early numbers as noisy and looking toward a much larger sample before drawing strong conclusions. Future posts will keep showing the small-n weeks as they are, including the rough ones.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: showing the rough weeks as they are is what will make the thread worth following. see you around trade 100.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
The cleanest test of Claude’s veto-only role is to retain every blocked setup and score it later using the exact entry, stop, target, spread, and expiry the EA would have used. Then report the base EA and post-veto stream side by side, including how many trades Claude blocked.

I’d also separate results by build. If the current version only began on 10 Oct, the week showing PF 4.44 largely reflects an earlier build, so combining it with future weeks could obscure whether the rules or veto behavior changed.

replies.author: Teh_Eno
replies.body:
Good points on both.

On the veto test: the plan (if the next logging upgrade goes in) is to keep every blocked setup with the EA’s exact entry, stop, target, spread and so on, plus a build stamp, so we can score them later and publish the base stream next to the post-veto stream, including how many Claude blocked. That side-by-side report isn’t live yet; it would come from that logged data.

On separating by build: agreed, and one correction — it isn’t a single build from 10 Oct onward. There were builds around 10/11 Oct, then a touch-input fix reload on 19 Oct, and a rollover-stop fix (r3) around 19–20 Oct. So any earlier PF figure belongs to its own build. Future posts I’ll split results by build stamp so rule or veto changes don’t get blurred together.

One nuance on “veto-only”: on LIVE Claude can only block, never create trades. On DEMO there’s an override that still takes some setups Claude scored low (score 4), so DEMO already partly looks like an unvetoed stream. LIVE and DEMO also use different touch limits and position caps, so they aren’t a clean A/B on the veto alone.

Happy to take more of this feedback — useful thread.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Posting the losing week and the PF with trade counts is the right way to do it, and saying the samples are small is honest. Two things would make the record easier to judge: because several builds shipped during the four weeks, the results are really a mix of versions, so I'd stamp each trade with the build number and report them separately. The Claude veto is the most testable part, since it only blocks trades: log every vetoed setup with its outcome had it been taken, so after a few dozen vetoes you can see whether the filter removes losers or just trims winners. Add spread and commission per trade and the average win and loss next to PF, since PF 4.44 on a handful of trades swings with one result. FX results also split around scheduled releases (NFP, CPI, rate decisions), and Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets around those dates.

replies.author: Teh_Eno
replies.body: Thanks, this is really helpful. You're right that the four weeks mix builds. I'll start stamping each trade with its build and break results out by version from here on. Logging vetoed setups with their "would-have" outcome is a great idea too, and it's the cleanest way to show whether the AI layer earns its keep, so I'll add that and report it once there are a few dozen vetoes. I'll also put average win/loss and costs next to PF in future updates, since you're right that PF swings a lot on this few trades. The EA already pauses new entries around NFP/CPI/rate decisions, but splitting results around those dates is a good extra check.
